form_value.sample_overlap.shares_participants_with: No other paper is identified as sharing participants. Within this paper, Experiment II reuses the 122 Experiment I teams; only its 139 individual participants are newly recruited.
form_value.participants.exclusions_excerpt: The 139 analyzed people are the newly recruited Experiment II individuals (p. 11; p. 36, Appendix A Table 3), who supplied 278 task outputs.
form_value.arms[0].description: One person working with ChatGPT4.0 on the same two tasks; 139 newly analyzed individuals and 278 outputs (p. 11; p. 36, Appendix A Table 3).

source_says.explanation: The source confirms enrollment and analysis of 139 individuals, plus reuse of the 122 Experiment I teams as comparators. It does not explicitly say that the individual cohort excludes previous Experiment I participants. Thus 139 is supported as the individual-arm count, but the categorical claim that these are 139 additional unique people is unsupported; this is not evidence that overlap actually occurred.

problems.quote: For the analysis, we employed OLS regression on a dataset that included 139 individuals from Experiment II and 122 teams from Experiment I, covering the two tasks.
problems.locator: PDF p. 11, Section 2.2, recruitment and analysis paragraphs; p. 36, Appendix A Table 3. Complete 55-page document, including both appendices, contains no explicit statement establishing nonoverlap of the two participant cohorts. Linked supplement/preregistration could not be accessed.

confirmed.statement: Experiment I randomized 435 people into 122 teams of three to five members, then randomized teams to AI conditions. Assignment headcounts are 142 human-only, 150 single-AI, and 143 multiple-AI.
confirmed.locator: PDF pp. 8-9, Section 2.1; p. 26, Figure 1 and its note.

confirmed.statement: The main Experiment I analysis includes all 122 teams, each completing two tasks: 244 output observations. Appendix A identifies 42/41/39 teams and 84/82/78 outputs in human-only/single-AI/multiple-AI order.
confirmed.locator: PDF pp. 10-11, Section 2.1; p. 34, Appendix A Table 1; pp. 37-38, Appendix B Tables 1-2, N rows.

confirmed.statement: Criterion 2 holds for Experiment I alone: the analyzed outputs represent all 122 distinct randomized human teams. Even the conservative lower bound of one contributing person per team exceeds 50; this does not require an exact analyzed headcount or adding Experiment II.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 9, allocation to teams; pp. 10-11, analyzed dataset; p. 34, Appendix A Table 1.

confirmed.statement: The PDF does not separately print post-exclusion person counts overall or by Experiment I arm, so the form appropriately leaves those analyzed-headcount fields null. No participant exclusions or participant attrition counts are described; Figure 1 is a design schematic, not a participant-flow report.
confirmed.locator: PDF pp. 8-11, methods; p. 26, Figure 1; pp. 34-55, Appendices A-B; full-document review.

confirmed.statement: The human-only teams received AI only after submitting the outputs used in analysis; the further refinement is expressly excluded. This is an excluded output phase, not an exclusion of those participants.

Experiment II explicitly analyzes 139 individuals producing 278 outputs. An individual-AI pair contains one human and one AI touchpoint; the two tasks and six ratings per output do not multiply the human participant count.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 5, definition of individual-AI pairs; p. 11, Section 2.2; p. 36, Appendix A Table 3.

confirmed.statement: Experiment II comparisons reuse the 122 Experiment I teams, giving 522 output observations together with the 139 individuals. The reused arms are not new randomized participants; no random assignment between individual and team conditions is described.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 11, Section 2.2; p. 21, post-hoc study description; p. 42, Appendix B Table 6.

confirmed.statement: Time regressions use 235 team-task outputs, 156 AI-team outputs, and 513 combined outputs; time-controlled performance models also use 513. These smaller Ns do not report how many people were lost or why observations were omitted.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 43, Appendix B Table 7, N row; p. 45, Table 9, N row; pp. 17-19, Section 3.2.6.

confirmed.statement: Matched comparisons use 110 and 154 output observations. Interaction analyses use 158 outputs, or 74 for multiple-AI interaction patterns; corresponding unique-person counts are unreported.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 19, matching and interaction methods; pp. 47-48, Appendix B Tables 11-12; pp. 49-51, Tables 13-15, N rows.

confirmed.statement: Team-process regressions use 122 teams or 80 AI teams. These Ns count teams, not additional people.
confirmed.locator: PDF pp. 52-53, Appendix B Tables 16-17, N rows; p. 20, Section 3.2.8.

confirmed.statement: The saved paper identifies no other paper as sharing these participants. This supports only the form wording that no other paper is identified, not a claim of demonstrated independence from all other samples.
confirmed.locator: Full saved PDF, pp. 1-55, including methods pp. 8-11, discussion pp. 21-22, and references pp. 22-25.

confirmed.statement: Both named OSF sources were requested with Python urllib and User-Agent atlas-screening/0.1; both failed with WinError 10013. They supply no verified additional participant-flow or sample-overlap evidence for this check.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 4, footnote 1, OSF 5su8c preregistration; p. 8, footnote 3, OSF zq48w supplementary materials; direct access attempts during this check.

summary: Experiment I independently meets the 50-person threshold, with all 122 randomized teams represented in the main analysis. The form treats the 139 Experiment II individuals as additional unique participants, but the source does not explicitly establish that they had not participated in Experiment I.
